title: Model Switchover & Fallback: Triage Runbook for Enterprise Support
author: Elena Martinez
body:
Summary
-------
This runbook describes the operational triage, model switchover, and fallback procedures to use during degraded model behavior, spike latency, or model availability loss for enterprise customers (Dedicated or Private). It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), SRE on-call, and Solutions Engineers performing operational support during a customer-facing incident.

When to use this runbook
-----------------------
Use this document when a customer reports one or more of the following:
- Significant increase in token latency (P95 or P99) for generation/chat endpoints beyond SLA thresholds.
- Consistent quality regressions or hallucinations after a model rollout.
- Errors related to model runtime (kernel OOMs, model load failures, KV cache corruption).
- Automatic fallback triggered by the routing layer and impacting request success rate.

Preconditions and prerequisites
-------------------------------
Before initiating switchover/fallback:
1. Confirm access: ensure you have redwood-console access and active SSH to the customer's Dedicated/private control plane (if applicable).
2. Identify customer configuration: model pinned version, route policy, cache keys, and any custom prehooks. See the customer’s route config in the Console: Routes > {customer} > {route-id}.
3. Check current SLOs and active incidents on status.redwood-internal: SLOs for this customer are typically:
   - Latency SLO: P95 < 800ms (hosted) / P95 < 1200ms (dedicated)
   - Error rate SLO: < 1% for 5m window
4. Notify stakeholders: CSE, SRE on-call, Account Manager (AM), and Product (if model regression suspected).

Ownership matrix
----------------
- CSE: customer communication, coordination, and runbook ops.
- SRE: runtime health checks, performing switchover commands, monitoring rollback safety.
- Solutions Eng: investigate prompt/regression and advise model/quantization changes.
- Product/Model Ops: invoked for suspected model quality regressions (A/B test data required).

Immediate triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
--------------------------------------------
1. Capture symptoms: collect sample requests/responses, timestamps, route-id, model name/version, and offtake rate.
2. Verify health: run quick health checks. Run from support workstation:
   - curl -sS -X GET "https://console.redwood/api/internal/health/{route-id}" | jq
   - Check runtime status: runbook-utils report-runtime {route-id} 
3. Confirm scope: is the issue per-customer, per-region, or global? Check metric dashboards:
   - Customer route dashboard: /console/dash/{route-id} > Last 60m
   - Global model healthboard: /console/dash/models/{model}"

(CONTINUED)
Detailed step-by-step switchover procedure
------------------------------------------
Use these steps to switch an affected route to a fallback model variant. Do not start without notifying AM & SRE.

1) Prepare fallback model variant
   - Identify approved fallback: look up the customer’s allowed model set in Console > Routes > {route-id} > "allowed_models". Typical fallback names: "gpt-like-3.5-v2-quant", "redwood-llm-slim-1.1".
   - Validate model binary: ensure the candidate is loaded on the target cluster by running: 
     rctl --cluster {cluster-name} list-models | grep {fallback-model}
2) Quiesce cache-sensitive requests (if applicable)
   - If prefix caching is active, enable read-only fallback for the route to avoid cache corruption: 
     rctl routes update {route-id} --cache-mode read-only --reason "fallback triggger"
3) Execute model switchover (can be automated via Console or CLI)
   - Console quick path: Routes > {route-id} > Edit > Model > Select {fallback-model} > Save & Canary 5% for 5 minutes.
   - CLI safe command (recommended for full automation):
     rctl routes rollout --route {route-id} --to {fallback-model} --strategy canary --canary-size 0.05 --canary-duration 300
4) Observe canary metrics (5–10 minutes)
   - Monitor: request latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, success rate, model output quality sample set.
   - Success criteria to promote: latency back within SLO AND error rate drop below 1% for 10m.
5) Promote or rollback
   - Promote: rctl routes rollout --route {route-id} --promote
   - Rollback: rctl routes rollback --route {route-id} --to {previous-model} --force --reason "canary-fail"

Safety & rollback considerations
--------------------------------
- Never promote if model outputs fail basic safety filters (see safety filter logs).
- If fallback increases hallucinations or changes customer SLA-significant output: escalate to Product immediately and revert to pinned model with controlled throttling.
- If KV cache integrity is suspect, perform cache flush for the route: 
  rctl cache flush --route {route-id} --confirm

Quick troubleshooting checklist (error classes)
------------------------------------------------
- High latency + increased tail tokens: check batching policies and kernel saturation.
  - Commands: ssh to runtime node and run: top/gpu-top; /usr/local/bin/runtime-inspect --tail-queue
- OOMs during model load: check model quantization variant and node free memory. If OOM, switch to smaller quantized variant.
- Route-level 5xx errors: check router-service logs for 502/504 patterns: 
  - kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/router-service --since=10m | grep "{route-id}" | head

Thresholds & quick reference table
----------------------------------
(Displayed as pipe table for quick reference)
| Metric | Alert threshold | Immediate action | Owner |
| Latency P95 | > 2x SLO for 5m | Initiate canary to fallback | SRE/CSE |
| Error rate | >= 2% for 5m | Immediate route canary to fallback | SRE |
| Model load failures | any model-load-failure | Disable autoscale, perform manual load | SRE + Model Ops |
| Safety filter blocks | > 0.5% of responses | Hold promotion, escalate to Product | Product/CSE |

Customer communication templates (short)
---------------------------------------
Use these statements in the first customer message while you triage:
- Acknowledgement: "We’ve received your report and are triaging with our SRE and Model Ops teams. We will update within 15 minutes with mitigation steps."
- During switchover: "We are routing a small portion of traffic to an alternate model variant to stabilize latency while we investigate. You may see minor differences in responses for a short period."
- Post-incident: Provide a short summary with root cause (if known), actions taken, and next steps (postmortem ETA).

Escalation matrix
------------------
1. SRE on-call (primary) — page: SRE-oncall@pagerduty — 0–15m
2. Model Ops (secondary) — page: model-ops@pagerduty — 15–60m
3. Product (for quality regressions) — @product-lead — 15–24h
4. Exec/Legal (if customer SLA breach & contractual exposure) — contact via AM — within 24h

Post-incident actions and RCA requirements
-----------------------------------------
- Required deliverables:
  1. Initial incident summary (within 4h) with timeline and mitigation.
  2. Full RCA (within 72h) including logs, canary graphs, samples of affected requests/responses, and suggested preventative measures.
  3. Action items with owners and deadlines (e.g., model rollback automation, expanded canary window).
- Add incident to customer QBR: include impact, duration, customer-reported severity, and improvements planned.

Monitoring playbook (what to watch)
-----------------------------------
- Dashboards to open:
  - Console > Dashboards > Route Overview ({route-id})
  - Console > Dashboards > Model Healthboard ({model})
  - Grafana: redwood/request-latency, redwood/error-rate, redwood/model-loads
- Logs: router-service, runtime-agent, model-loader, safety-filter
- Alerting channels: #incidents, SRE-pagerduty, CSE-team slack channel

Related artifacts & links
-------------------------
- Route config schema: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/route-config-schema
- Canary rollout CLI reference: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/rollout-cli-usage
- Model approval list (customer-specific): Console > Customers > {customer-id} > Approved Models

Appendix: sample CLI snippets
----------------------------
1) Start a 5% canary to fallback model: 
   rctl routes rollout --route r-abc123 --to redwood-llm-slim-1.1 --strategy canary --canary-size 0.05 --canary-duration 300 --reason "support-triage-2026-01-12"
2) Promote canary after success:
   rctl routes rollout --route r-abc123 --promote
3) Rollback to previous model immediately:
   rctl routes rollback --route r-abc123 --to redwood-llm-recent-3.0 --force --reason "rollback-on-failed-canary"

Contact list (internal)
-----------------------
- CSE on-call: cse-oncall@redwood.com
- SRE on-call: sre-oncall@redwood.com
- Model Ops: model-ops@redwood.com
